defects.title: pre-Sierra macOS versions with a patch number or a one-digit minor select postSierra
defects.trigger:
CBTDIR = temp folder with binary/maci64/bin/preSierra and postSierra (both on path); fake sw_vers first on PATH printing 'ProductName:	Mac OS X
ProductVersion:	10.11.6
BuildVersion:	15G31
'; adaptMacPath()
defects.observed: postSierra on the path, preSierra removed for ProductVersion 10.11.6, 10.9.5 and 10.9 (preSierra only for 10.11): str2double('10.11.6') = NaN and NaN < 10.12 is false; 10.9 > 10.12 as a decimal
defects.expected: preSierra for every version below 10.12 (help: 'Sierra/High Sierra or higher and Anything below'); compare version components

notes: Repro (MATLAB, Unix): global CBTDIR; d = tempname; b = fullfile(d,'binary','maci64','bin'); mkdir(fullfile(b,'preSierra')); mkdir(fullfile(b,'postSierra')); f = fullfile(d,'fakebin'); mkdir(f); fid = fopen(fullfile(f,'sw_vers'),'w'); fprintf(fid,'#!/bin/sh\nprintf "ProductName:\\tMac OS X\\nProductVersion:\\t10.11.6\\nBuildVersion:\\t15G31\\n"\n'); fclose(fid); system(['chmod +x ' fullfile(f,'sw_vers')]); old = CBTDIR; CBTDIR = d; setenv('PATH',[f pathsep getenv('PATH')]); adaptMacPath(); contains(path, 'postSierra') -> postSierra added, preSierra removed. (Restore PATH, path, CBTDIR.) Flag external-program: sw_vers exists only on macOS; a fake sw_vers on PATH (as testAddKeyToKnownHosts does for ssh-keyscan) reaches every line, so the row would be fully testable on Unix once fixed. Callers: none in the ledger (sw_vers missing on Linux gives status 127, oldMac = true).
confirmed_by: lead (source read: str2double('10.11.6') is NaN and 10.9 > 10.12 numerically, lines 20-21, so older versions get postSierra)

notes: Fake CBTDIR in tempname with a hand-built binary/<arch>/bin and lib tree; asserts exact PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH suffixes (subfolders compared as a set: rdir order). Second call appends duplicates (no check), pinned. PATH, LD_LIBRARY_PATH and CBTDIR restored. Declares needsUnix (Unix variables asserted); line 25 is the ispc branch. rdir is external/base/utilities/rdir (not src).

CellNetAnalyzer not installed: a stub startcna.m in tempname with code/ext/libSBML (+subfolder) and code/ext/efmtool on the path reaches the installed branch and the two rmpath branches. Any real startcna is rmpath'ed first; line 26 reached by rmpath(genpath(CBTDIR/external/analysis/CnaCobraInterface)) before the call. MATLAB path saved and restored with path(savedPath). Legacy testConvertCNAModelToCbModel.m (testIO) also calls checkCNAinstallation but tests the converter, so this new file does not duplicate it.

Fake CBTDIR in tempname holding a hand-written .gitignore (comments, indented comment, blank and whitespace-only lines, padded entries); expected lists by hand. CBTDIR restored. Not tested (undocumented): a missing .gitignore makes fopen return -1 and feof errors.

Unix behaviour is the documented error 'gitBash can only be installed on Windows.' (verifyCobraFunctionError with 0 and 2 outputs). Declares needsUnix. Windows branch exempt (OS-specific); it calls getsysenvironvar (not found under src/, Windows only). The function declares global gitBashVersion: new globals are cleared at the end.

defects.title: only the first column of a 'G' row is negated
defects.trigger: LP.A = sparse([1 2; 3 4]); LP.b = [5; 6]; LP.c = [1; 1]; LP.lb = [0; 0]; LP.ub = [10; 10]; LP.csense = ['G'; 'L']; LP.osense = 1; convertCobraLP2mps(LP, 'conv')
defects.observed: conv.mps row LE1 = -1*X1 + 2*X2 with RHS -5 (i.e. -x1 + 2x2 <= -5): line 72 A2(G) = -A2(G) uses the m x 1 logical G as a linear index into the first column only
defects.expected: -x1 - 2x2 <= -5 (whole G row negated, as line 73 does for b and as writeLPProblem writes for the same LP)

notes: Repro: the TRIGGER in a temp folder, then disp(fileread('conv.mps')) -> 'X1 COST 1 LE1 -1' and 'X2 COST 1 LE1 2', RHS LE1 -5. Fix: A2(G, :) = -A2(G, :). Correct whenever every G row is zero outside column 1. No callers in src/ or test/ (grep). Uses findstr (deprecated) on lines 59-61. BuildMPS/SaveMPS are external/base/io/BuildMPS (not src).
confirmed_by: lead (source read: A2(G) = -A2(G) with a logical row mask indexes linearly, line 72, so only the first column of each G row is negated)

notes: GAMS not installed: a test double wgdx.m (written to a tempname folder, added to the path, path restored) saves its arguments to a .mat file, so every line is reached and the GDX symbols (names, order S,isRev,rxn,met,lb,ub, full S, uels, isRev = lb<0, form/type) and the help text are asserted against hand-written values; any real wgdx is rmpath'ed first for the 'wgdx() not found' branch. Not a defect (NOTE says wgdx is required) but worth knowing: without wgdx, h = writeGDXFromCOBRA(model) errors 'Output argument "helpText" ... not assigned'. The lead may prefer to treat the wgdx double as out of policy; if so, lines 59-108 would be exempt as 'needs GAMS'.

defects.title: the outputFormat option always fails validation
defects.trigger: LP as in convertCobraLP2mps row; writeLPProblem(LP, 'outputFormat', 'mps')
defects.observed: error "The value of 'outputFormat' is invalid. Not enough input arguments." (validator on line 84 calls strcmpi(acceptedTypes) with one argument); same for positional writeLPProblem(LP, 'p1', 'f1', struct(), 'mps')
defects.expected: 'mps' accepted (documented as the supported default): any(strcmpi(x, acceptedTypes))

defects.title: writeMatrix given as the first option is taken for a positional problem name
defects.observed: error "The value of 'fileName' is invalid. It must satisfy the function: ischar." ('writeMatrix' missing from optionalArgumentList, line 57, so lines 66-75 rewrite it as problemName/fileName)
defects.expected: documented name-value parameter accepted in any position

defects.title: vartype is dropped from the default output
defects.observed: BOUNDS 'UP BND1 X1 10' (continuous); with 'solverParams', struct('x', 1) the same problem gives 'UI BND1 X1 10'. Line 206 calls BuildMPS without the Integer/Binary lists built on lines 186-187
defects.expected: .vartype is documented as 'used to build the integer/binary index lists passed to the MPS writer'

notes: Quarantine scope for the lead: the outputFormat and writeMatrix-first defects are confined to call forms none of the src callers use (solveCobraLP lines 394/1528, solveCobraQP 875, solveCobraMILP 468 pass problemName/fileName/solverParams by name); the vartype defect reaches only callers that pass a vartype without solverParams (solveCobraMILP passes solverParams, so it takes the line-209 path that keeps integers). Legacy testMPS.m (testMPS) calls writeLPProblem together with solveCobraLP/solveCobraMILP 'mps' paths; it is not a dedicated test, so this file was created. Also noted, not filed: 'writeMatrix' doc says 'only write the Matrix, not the full problem' but both branches write a full MPS; getDefaultCompartmentSymbols outputs (line 79) are unused.
confirmed_by: lead (writer's MATLAB reproductions: outputFormat unusable, writeMatrix first fails, vartype dropped without solverParams)

defects.title: integerizeS is called with a matrix but needs a model structure
defects.observed: error 'Dot indexing is not supported for variables of this type.' in integerizeS line 39; line 17 passes the matrix SeFull
defects.expected: the documented 'full stoichiometric matrix' is integerised and written, e.g. via integerizeS(struct('S', SeFull), 0, 0).S

notes: Repro: write4ti2([1 -1; 0 1], 'x', 0). Further defects visible only by reading (unreachable behind line 17, so not confirmed in MATLAB and not filed): (1) uni is documented optional (default 0) but has no default, so write4ti2(S, f) would fail on line 21; (2) the 'end' on line 44 closes the if/else, so line 45 fclose(fid) runs after line 32 fclose(fid) in the uni == 0 branch (closing a closed fid errors); (3) uni = 1 writes int2str(nRxn/2), which is wrong for odd nRxn. No callers in src/.
confirmed_by: lead (source read: integerizeS(SeFull) passes a matrix, line 17; integerizeS takes a model)

defects.title: text values of problemTypeParams.method have no effect for MIQP
defects.trigger: cp.setDefault = []; cp.Param = struct(); cp.DisplayFunc = @disp; ptp = struct('printLevel',0,'logFile',0,'feasTol',1e-6,'optTol',1e-6,'relMipGapTol',1e-4,'intTol',1e-5,'absMipGapTol',0,'timeLimit',100,'method','PRIMAL'); out = setCplexParametersForProblem(cp, ptp, struct(), 'MIQP')
defects.observed: out.Param.lpmethod.Cur = 4 for 'PRIMAL' (and every text value): lines 248-260 set lpmethod, then line 302 (else of the 'LP' test on line 268) resets it to 4 for every non-LP problem type
defects.expected: documented '.method - LP/QP algorithm selector used when problemType is MIQP (numeric legacy code, or AUTOMATIC/PRIMAL/...)': PRIMAL selects algorithm 1; numeric values do take effect (method 0 -> qpmethod 1)

notes: CPLEX not installed (exist('Cplex','class') = 0); a struct with setDefault/Param/DisplayFunc stands in (as testSetCplexParam.m does) and reached the defect. Quarantine scope for the lead: confined to problemType 'MIQP' with a text problemTypeParams.method, i.e. only solveCobraMIQP (line 295); solveCobraLP/QP/MILP pass 'LP'/'QP'/'MILP' and do not reach it. Also noted, not filed: line 262's error says 'solverParams.lpmethod' for problemTypeParams.method (cosmetic); numeric MIQP method -1 sets qpmethod -1, not a CPLEX qpmethod value (unconfirmable without CPLEX); line 355 isfield(cplexProblem,'Start') is always false for a real Cplex object (isfield on objects), so advance start is never set (unconfirmable without CPLEX); setCplexParam is only called inside 'if 0' (line 376), so the ledger edge to setCplexParam is dead code.
confirmed_by: lead (source read: for MIQP a text method is overwritten by lpmethod 4, line 302)
